note: The ANATOMY crosswalk as data: each cut (one of the Matter of Britain's seven organs) maps to each voice's distinct take, with an optional quote_id into quotes.json. quote_id=null means that voice's take is described from the canon, not quoted (often because the relevant text is off-corpus — see ANATOMY.md coverage map). Voices match base.json render_order. Discipline: name the version, never flatten it.

source-of-rule.gloss: Where legitimate kingship comes from — conferred, seized, proven, or fated.

Geoffrey of Monmouth.term: descent + conquest; Caliburn forged in Avalon

The Chroniclers.term: Nennius's twelve battles; the pseudo-historical Arthur (Gildas names Badon, not Arthur)

The Gawain Romances.term: Dame Ragnelle's riddle — sovereignty inverted to the marriage-bed

the-fellowship.gloss: The order built against precedence and to bind violence — and the flaw it cannot remove.

Malory.term: the Pentecostal Oath, and its breach by the best knights

Chrétien de Troyes.term: the knight audited against the code

The Vulgate.term: the kin-network whose loyalty turns on itself

The Chroniclers.term: Wace invents the Round Table — equality against precedence

The Gawain Romances.term: the code tried on one knight; the green girdle (SGGK)

the-grail.gloss: The highest good, and whether reaching for it perfects the kingdom or depletes it.

Wolfram von Eschenbach.term: a stone; the wound healed by compassion (Anfortas)

The Vulgate.term: the Holy Vessel; the seed of judgment-by-purity

Chrétien de Troyes.term: the open Grail; the unasked question of attention (Perceval, off-corpus)

Malory.term: the Grail enters Camelot, then the quest empties the fellowship

The Mabinogion.term: Peredur's bleeding spear, unasked (the Welsh Grail)

The Grail Romances.term: the Queste — judgment by purity (+ Perlesvaus, the militant Grail)

courtly-love.gloss: The love that is the glory of the court and the bomb beneath its floor.

Chrétien de Troyes.term: love overrides reason and shame (the Cart)

Malory.term: tragic; defends the old love even as it dooms the court

Gottfried von Strassburg.term: the love potion — love as fate, not choice

the-wound-and-wasteland.gloss: Sovereignty as a body; the king's wound is the land's famine — sacral kingship, a medieval analogue to (not identical with) Kantorowicz's king's two bodies.

Malory.term: the Dolorous Stroke lays three kingdoms waste

Wolfram von Eschenbach.term: Anfortas, wounded for love, healed by pity

once-and-future.gloss: Deferred restoration; messianic time — sovereignty held in suspension.

Geoffrey of Monmouth.term: borne to Avalon 'for the healing of his wounds' — not said to die

Malory.term: rex quondam rexque futurus, reported not endorsed

The Chroniclers.term: Wace's 'hope of Britain'; Layamon's Argante bears him to Avalon

foreknowledge-and-doom.gloss: The hinge: who knows the end, why knowing it changes nothing, and what is lost as the magic fades.

Geoffrey of Monmouth.term: prophecy as dynastic charter (the Boar of Cornwall)

Malory.term: the seer undone by the enchantment he foresaw (Nimue)
